A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same alignment-stage research despite the changed title and format. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original DPO and SLiC-HF training results, AlpacaEval evaluations, boundary-score measurements, and preference-data analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds diversity-analysis curves for additional model configurations and on-policy comparisons.

M1.justification: The two-stage framework and Algorithm 1 retain the same pairwise preference comparisons, vote accumulation, and stage-selection rule. Reorganizing the explanation and omitting the SLiC-HF loss formula do not establish a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: UltraChat, UltraFeedback, and AlpacaEval retain their training and evaluation roles. The additional Qwen configurations extend an existing analysis without introducing new datasets, task requirements, or test environments.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds PC_on as a reference comparator alongside PC_off and PC_llama in the diversity analysis. The principal benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged; SLiC-HF was already evaluated in v1 Appendix D.2.

E3.justification: The diversity diagnostic expands from Zephyr-7B to include Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen3-4B. The computational-cost discussion also changes the stated DPO training size from 63,967 to 61,135 samples. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Expanded Figure 3 checks whether the diversity contrast persists across additional models and whether PC_llama resembles on-policy data. This strengthens an existing supplementary analysis. The distribution-distinctness check and SLiC-HF generalizability analysis are retained, with the latter moved into Section 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional Figure 3 curves are training trajectories, not new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds on-policy trajectories and results for two additional model configurations. The benchmark scores in Tables 1–4 and the relocated SLiC-HF table remain unchanged. Table 2 drops average-length results, including the PC_llama values 1,223 and 2,666.

T1.justification: The central definitions, Theorems 5.1, 5.2, and 5.4, and their proofs are retained. However, v1 Appendix D.2's explicit mathematical definition of the SLiC-HF objective, Eq. (25), is omitted. This is a limited removal of mathematical specification, not evidence of a changed objective.

C1.justification: The contribution list removes v1's explicit claim to be the first systematic account of alignment stages and emphasizes the observed effectiveness discrepancy. The central claims about two stages, diversity versus quality, and boundary measurement remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.5 adds an interpretation of the similar PC_on and PC_llama trajectories as support for the comparison design. Section 7 shifts future-work emphasis from reward over-optimization and sample efficiency to adaptive data blending. The discretization-based explanation linking diversity to preference approximation in v1 Section 5.1 is removed.

D1.justification: The computational-cost passage revises the training count and estimated overhead from about 3% to 3.2%, without explaining the count change. The SLiC-HF loss and parameter explanations are removed. A new reproducibility statement mainly points to existing details; the hardware and hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix B.6 relates the work to LUFFY, Qwen3, SFT/RL curricula, and RLVR/offline-RL research. SimPO is newly cited, while the REINFORCE reference is removed. These additions broaden context while retaining the original iterative-DPO and candidate-diversity positioning.

P1.justification: The title and author list change, contributions and conclusion are rewritten, and boundary-measurement material is consolidated in Section 5. Existing SLiC-HF discussion moves into Section 6, and short disclosure sections are added. Most substantive prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column conference formatting, with major result tables reorganized into side-by-side model blocks. Figure 3 becomes a three-panel plot, Figure 4 adds an explanatory diagram, and Table 10 abbreviates example responses. These constitute substantial visual and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: Expanded Figure 3 provides a more direct check of PC_llama's role as a diversity control across models, while the reorganized boundary discussion and new Figure 4 clarify the argument. These are useful but limited gains because the core method, benchmark results, and proofs remain unchanged. Benefits are tempered by omitted SLiC-HF details and the unexplained training-count revision.
